ledger.x: 822: the Moravians first appear in the record, paying tribute to Louis the Pious.

c. 833: Mojmír I drives Pribina out of Nitra and unites it with Moravia. Mojmír expelled 'one Pribina' across the Danube and Pribina 'fled to Ratpot who administered the March of Pannonia from around 833'; 'conquered the neighbouring principality of Nitra' in the early 830s. c. 872: Duke Bořivoj of Bohemia is recognised by his overlord Svatopluk. 'In this era Bohemia was subordinated to Great Moravia' and Bořivoj was 'recognised as such around 872 by his overlord King Svatopluk I of Moravia'; the Duchy of Bohemia page: 'formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm'.…

c. 874-879: Svatopluk subjugates the Vistulans. Vistulans page: 'Probably around 874 they were subjugated by king Svatopluk I of Moravia', and a cited source has their 'annexation to the Great Moravian Empire between Ad 875-879'; the same page adds 'no conclusive evidence exists to prove this theory' and does not say…

c. 875 in Cliopatria; the page puts Silesia and Lusatia later. Great Moravia page: Silesia and Lusatia 'probably' annexed 'in the early 890s' (Bartl); Mojmir II page: 'Lusatia followed suit in 897' (when it seceded). 882: Svatopluk's forces invade the March of Pannonia in the Wilhelminer War.
Late 885: peace with East Francia ends the Wilhelminer War.
Winter 890: the Bohemian duchy passes under Svatopluk's direct rule (see the gain below).
Winter 890: after Arnulf's agreement Svatopluk rules Bohemia himself.
June 895: the Bohemian dukes swear fealty to Arnulf and leave the Moravian realm.
896: the Hungarians cross the Carpathians into the eastern lands of Moravia.
896: the northern lands drop away after Svatopluk's death.
898: Nitra leaves direct Moravian rule as an appanage (new state 'nitra', founded 898 with great-moravia as counterpart).
898: Nitra becomes a separate appanage under Svatopluk's other heir, still tied to Moravia.
900: the Hungarian army 'attacked and invaded' Moravia.
900: Moravia shrinks to 20,901 km2.
902: the fighting ends with a Hungarian victory over Great Moravia.
902: the Hungarians occupy Great Moravia's eastern area.
906/907: Nitra's tie to Moravia ends as the Hungarians take the land.

c. 907: Great Moravia ends. wars.name: Louis the German's campaign against Rastislav (855)
wars.outcome: The Frankish army 'foundered before the walls of one of Rastislav's strongholds' in 855 and withdrew; Rastislav raided the Danube estates.

wars.name: Louis the German's invasion of Moravia (864)
wars.outcome: In August 864 Louis besieged Dowina (Devín); 'Unable to escape the Frankish siege, Rastislav surrendered', gave hostages and swore a new oath of suzerainty.

wars.name: Frankish invasions and Svatopluk's revolt (869-872)
wars.outcome: Frankish troops invaded both Moravian realms in August 869; in 870 Svatopluk seized Rastislav and handed him to Carloman; arrested in 871, Svatopluk was freed and drove out the Franks; in 872 Louis's armies were forced to withdraw.

wars.name: Wilhelminer War
wars.outcome: Svatopluk intervened as an ally of the Wilhelminers against the margrave Aribo; Pannonia east of the Rába was devastated.

wars.name: Arnulf's invasion of Moravia (892)
wars.outcome: 'Svatopluk, however, broke his pledges, so Arnulf decided to invade Moravia in 891'; 'Arnulf's invasion started in July 892, but he failed to defeat Svatopluk.'

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin
wars.outcome: The Hungarians raided Pannonia in 894, 'attacked and invaded' Moravia in 900, and in 902 defeated Great Moravia and occupied its eastern area; the state ended between 902 and 907.

certainty.note: The Great Moravia page: Moravia's borders 'cannot be exactly determined'.
